# Interface surface tension from the parachor (Weinaug-Katz)

`eos.parachor_mixture_surface_tension`

## Source

**NeqSim master `ParachorSurfaceTension`**

`calcSurfaceTension(interface1, interface2)`, the mixture form, reached through `InterfaceProperties`' three interface calculators.

DOI: [10.1021/ie50398a028](https://doi.org/10.1021/ie50398a028)


## What this model is

A **direct** model: a computation over vectors, with no iteration and therefore no algorithm block. It is here because a calculation's inputs are scalars, so a composition vector has nowhere in the calc registry to go - and it is a model rather than a library function so that it goes through the spec-driven pipeline like everything else.

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `parachors` | dimensionless | each component's `PARACHOR`, in NeqSim's mixed unit `(mN/m)**(1/4) * cm**3/mol`; the `1e-6` in the formula converts its `cm**3/mol` to `m**3/mol`. **Declared dimensionless** because no vocabulary unit expresses a fractional power of a non-SI unit. |
| `rho_gas` | kg/m**3 | the gas phase's mass density. |
| `M_gas` | kg/mol | the gas phase's molar mass; `rho/M` is its molar density. |
| `x_gas` | dimensionless | the gas phase's mole fractions, in the same order as `parachors`. |
| `rho_liquid` | kg/m**3 | the liquid (or aqueous) phase's mass density. |
| `M_liquid` | kg/mol | the liquid phase's molar mass. |
| `x_liquid` | dimensionless | the liquid phase's mole fractions, in the same order as `parachors`. |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sigma` | N/m | the interface's surface tension: `1e-3 * sum(...)**4`, the `1e-3` recovering `N/m` from `(mN/m)**(1/4)` to the fourth. |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `rho_gas > 0` | raises | a phase with no density has no interface to be in tension; the class would divide by it, catch the exception and answer zero |
| `rho_liquid > 0` | raises | the liquid's density is the sum's positive term |
| `M_gas > 0` | raises | `rho/M` divides by it |
| `M_liquid > 0` | raises | `rho/M` divides by it |

## Assumptions

- **the pair's form, not the pure component's.** `eos.parachor_surface_tension` ports `calcPureComponentSurfaceTension`, where the mole fractions divide out; this one sums `P_i (rho_l/M_l x_l_i - rho_g/M_g x_g_i)`, a per-component molar-density difference.

- **the gas is the negative term.** `calcSurfaceTension(interface1, interface2)` subtracts `interface1`'s contribution, and `InterfaceProperties.getSurfaceTension` passes the gas first - so it is the order the class calls its two phases in and not a sign the arithmetic proves.

- **one calculator serves all three interfaces.** The dispatch picks `gasLiquidSurfaceTensionCalc`, `gasAqueousSurfaceTensionCalc` or `liquidLiquidSurfaceTensionCalc` by the two phase types, and all three default to `ParachorSurfaceTension`, so a gas/oil and a gas/aqueous pair are one arithmetic here.

- **a non-positive density or molar mass is refused**, where the class catches the arithmetic exception and answers `0.0` - a silent zero that reads as a tension of zero rather than as a failure.

- **a single-phase system is not this id's state.** The class returns `0.0` when the system has fewer than two phases; one phase has no interface, so that is a caller's refusal rather than a tension.

- the length of `parachors` must match both compositions; the class sums over the first phase's component count and would throw on a mismatch.

## References

- NeqSim - https://github.com/equinor/neqsim - Apache-2.0. `physicalproperties/interfaceproperties/surfacetension/ParachorSurfaceTension.java` is the port source, through `InterfaceProperties.getSurfaceTension`.
- Weinaug, C. F.; Katz, D. L. (1943). \"Surface tensions of methane-propane mixtures.\" Ind. Eng. Chem. 35(2), 239-246. DOI 10.1021/ie50398a028. The parachor form for a mixture, which the pure-component Macleod-Sugden relation is the one-component case of.
- `validation/neqsim/ParachorProbe.java` and `captures/parachor_probe.tsv` - four rows: two gas/oil pairs of two and three components, and two gas/aqueous pairs, printing every input the sum reads.
